instructions: Crush the cumin seeds with the flat of a knife or a mortar. Mince the onion to make 1/4 cup, grate 2 tsp of the ginger, chop the curry leaves and chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro.

In a large bowl, whisk the ragi flour, rice flour, salt, cumin and pepper. Add 2 cups of water and whisk until it's smooth. Whisk in 2 more cups of water. The batter should be thin and pourable, like thin cream.
Stir in the onion, ginger, curry leaves and cilantro. Leave the batter for 15 minutes.
Heat a large nonstick or cast iron pan over medium-high heat until a few drops of water sizzle and disappear. If you have a second pan, heat it too so you can cook two at a time.

Stir the batter well, since the flour sinks to the bottom. Pour about 1/3 cup into the pan in a thin circle, starting at the edge and working in toward the center. Don't spread it. Fill any big gaps with a spoonful of batter.
Drizzle 1 tsp of the oil around the edge. Cook for 3 minutes, until the edges lift from the pan and the underside is golden and crisp.
Flip it and cook for 1 minute. Transfer to a plate.
Stir the batter and make sure the pan is hot again before each dosa. This makes about 12. Serve hot.
method_notes: Swasthi's Recipes (4.97 from 104 ratings) is the lead: a thin batter of ragi flour, rice flour and water with onion, ginger, curry leaves and cumin, rested for a few minutes and poured into a hot pan in a ring without spreading. My Food Story's version is the same idea with a 30 minute rest. Semolina is optional in both and is left out here to keep it gluten-free, and oil replaces the ghee to keep it dairy-free. A black pepper pinch stands in for the green chili.
